reason: The cited evidence discusses general principles of protective oxide formation (E1, E2) and corrosion/passivation in HEAs (E3), but none provides specific data on microsegregation-driven oxidation in additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 or directly links microsegregation to non-uniform scale formation and spallation. The key premises about microsegregation effects and homogenization benefits are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Microsegregation in as-built AM HEA causes non-uniform elemental distribution of Ti and Cr
Local Ti/Cr enrichment leads to heterogeneous, less protective oxide nucleation and growth
Non-uniform oxide scale is more prone to spallation and degradation
Homogenization reduces microsegregation, enabling uniform distribution of reactive elements
Uniform distribution fosters a continuous, adherent protective oxide film with slower degradation
